Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting & network constraints — call recap and next steps

Hi Chris — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and a clear next step list. I captured the items we discussed and what MedSecure is prioritizing.

High-level goals
- Move to a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) to satisfy regulatory and data residency requirements.
- Keep inference latency under 250ms p95 for user-facing flows.
- Ensure auditability (retention of logs + access reviews) for SOC/compliance audits.

Primary pain points you stated
1) Network egress restrictions — all traffic must originate from MedSecure-owned subnets and only talk to approved endpoints.
2) HSM/KMS requirements — keys must be customer-managed; your security team requires HSM-backed KMS with split-key control.
3) Air-gap considerations for an eventual offline sync process — procurement is asking about how model updates are delivered in an air-gapped environment.
4) Procurement timeline — legal/procurement needs artifacts (SOC 2, data flow diagram, exception policy) to begin review next week.

What Redwood can provide (agreed items)
- A private control plane deployment (VPC peering or dedicated on-prem appliance) with network allowlist options. See the attached high-level architecture (redwood-private-arch.png).
- KMS integrations: we can support customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS + HSM-backed options) and provide a short KMS integration checklist.
- Evidence pack: SOC2 summary + audit log retention description (attached SOC2-summary.pdf).
- Networking checklist for the NetOps team that lists ports, IP ranges and proxying options (attached networking-checklist.xlsx).

Open questions / asks for MedSecure (next actions)
- Please share the NetOps point of contact and the preferred method to exchange temporary test credentials (VPN jumpbox vs. bastion).
- Confirm whether a VPC peering model or an on-prem appliance is preferred for initial pilot (I heard peering is favored, but procurement asked for both options).
- Procurement requested a contact and an estimated MSA timeline target — what cutoff date should we aim for to support your Q3 pilot?

Proposed next steps
1) NetOps sync (30–45 min) to validate the network checklist and confirm firewall/proxy constraints. I suggest Wed 2 Jul or Thu 3 Jul — please confirm.
2) We will deliver a one-page KMS/HSM note by EOD Wed (Jonas will own the doc).
3) Redwood will provide a short list of model update delivery options for air-gapped sites (inline vs. offline bundle).

If that all looks right I can schedule the NetOps call — looping in Jonas and Ben to coordinate the technical handoff.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting & network constraints — call recap and next steps

Hi Naomi — appreciate the clear write-up, thank you. Confirming a few items from our side and adding procurement/ops asks.

Confirmations
- We are leaning toward VPC peering initially for the pilot to avoid appliance procurement lead times, but we need the appliance option documented for long-term planning.
- HSM-backed KMS is a hard requirement for production; pilot may use cloud KMS with strict IAM.

Procurement asks
- SOC2 Type II report — procurement needs either the full report under NDA or the SOC2 summary and a point of contact who can handle an evidence request. We will request the full report if available.
- Standard MSA and sample SOW timeline — procurement asked if Redwood has a template and an estimated signature window (we're looking at 4–6 weeks once internal review starts).

NetOps/Technical notes
- Firewalling: our NetOps will require a list of source IPs (or a CIDR range) for outbound calls, and support for mutual TLS is preferred for service-to-service.
- Air-gap delivery: for now we want a documented process for secure offline model bundle delivery, checksum verification and manual install steps.

Next steps from MedSecure
1) I'll introduce our NetOps engineer (Alyssa Ng) to your NetOps contact — expect an intro by EOD Tue.
2) Procurement will reach out separately to request the SOC2 evidence and MSA template.

Thanks again; we should be able to confirm the NetOps meeting once Alyssa is looped in.

—Chris

Head of Infrastructure, MedSecure
